A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fast3R. All 16 pages of each version, including supplementary material, were readable; equations, tables, figures, and relocated content support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Fast3R pose estimation, reconstruction, inference-efficiency, ablation, and dynamic-scene results, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original Fast3R experiments and adds RealEstate10K pose results, multi-view depth evaluation, and a Lighthouse reconstruction comparison.

M1.justification: The encoder–fusion–dual-head pipeline, pointmap losses, randomized image-index embeddings, and pose/ICP inference procedures remain unchanged. The larger reported ViT configurations concern model-size settings under E3; no new method component is introduced.

E1.justification: Training adds BlendedMVS and MegaDepth, expanding outdoor coverage. Evaluation adds RealEstate10K pose estimation and multi-view depth estimation on ScanNet, ETH3D, DTU, and Tanks & Temples. The dynamic-scene experiments are retained in Appendix F.1, not removed.

E2.justification: The new depth comparison introduces COLMAP-DENSE alongside DUSt3R at two resolutions, and Figure 13 adds a qualitative comparison against Spann3R on Lighthouse. Comparator membership in the existing pose and reconstruction tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 3.3–4 revise the reported configurations from ViT-Base to ViT-Large, including 12 to 24 fusion layers. Training changes from 6.5K to 174K steps, batch size 64 to 128, and 512×512 images to 512 pixels on the longest side. These are substantive reported setting changes; they do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds a comparison of training with versus without the outdoor datasets, and Figure 13 adds the Lighthouse case study. Existing view-count, positional-embedding, local-head, model/data-scaling, and bundle-adjustment analyses remain. The expanded local-head discussion clarifies an existing comparison with unchanged numerical evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Retained plots and newly added result tables introduce no change in statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains v1's CO3D RRA@15/mAA values of 99.7/82.5 as Fast3R-no-outdoor and adds the differently trained default model at 96.2/75.0, with RealEstate10K mAA 72.7. Table 7 adds depth results across four datasets, and Figure 13 adds qualitative evidence. Existing Tables 2–6 retain their numerical values; textual speedup ratios change from 200×/700× to 320×/1000×.

T1.justification: The pointmap definitions and Equations 1–4 are mathematically unchanged. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added; the expanded local-head explanation is conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about single-pass reconstruction, scaling with views, accuracy, and throughput. The 99.7% CO3D claim remains, with its supporting result identified as Fast3R-no-outdoor in v2.

C2.justification: v2 replaces speculation that the local head may eventually become unnecessary with an explanation based on anchor-invariant local targets. It adds the outdoor-generalization versus CO3D-accuracy tradeoff and changes the example view count associated with drift from over 200 to over 300.

D1.justification: v2 substantially revises the training recipe and documents encoder patch size, head initialization, custom multi-view loading, and 128 A100-80GB GPUs instead of 64 A100s. It removes v1's scene/video counts and 7% CO3D disclosure. Reproducibility remains ambiguous because Appendix A still specifies ViT-Base for all main experiments, contradicting v2's ViT-Large specification.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting MegaDepth, BlendedMVS, and RealEstate10K and removes the BERT reference. Positioning relative to DUSt3R, MASt3R, Spann3R, and traditional reconstruction pipelines is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the architecture details and local-head discussion, adds a short scaling summary in Section 5.2, and moves the 4D reconstruction section to Appendix F.1. Most explanatory prose and the principal narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The displays undergo substantial reorganization: Table 1 gains a benchmark column and model row, Table 5 clarifies its row labels, and Table 7 and Figure 13 are added. Existing supplementary figures are extensively rearranged, while the small main-text DAVIS display becomes a full-width appendix figure. These are layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 provides broader evidence through RealEstate10K and depth evaluation and resolves unclear wording around the local-head comparison. However, its revised ViT-Large specification conflicts with Appendix A's retained ViT-Base statement, leaving the configuration behind retained results unresolved. The added empirical and explanatory value coexists with a material reproducibility problem, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
